summary.en: Later Zhou-era geography notes that descendant marquises from Taihao still survived.
Later Zhou-era geography notes that descendant lines from the Yellow Emperor still survived.
Tang (Yao) marquises were said still to survive in later records.
Yu (Shun) marquises were said still to survive in later records.

units.zh: 昔在黃帝，作舟車以濟不通，旁行天下，方制萬里，畫野分州，得百里之國萬區。
units.en: In antiquity under the Yellow Emperor, boats and carts were devised to bridge impassable routes; he ranged across the realm, fixed the standard measure at ten thousand li, mapped the land and divided it into provinces, and thereby obtained ten thousand hundred-li states.
units.literal: In former times under the Yellow Emperor, boats and carts were made to cross what could not be crossed; he traveled the realm on all sides, set the square measure at ten thousand li, mapped the wilds and divided provinces, and obtained ten thousand states of a hundred li each.

units.zh: 是故易稱「先王以建萬國，親諸侯」，《書》云「協和萬國」，此之謂也。
units.en: Thus the Changes says, "The former kings established myriad states and kept the feudal lords close," and the Book of Documents says, "They harmonized the myriad states"—that is what this refers to.
units.literal: Thus the Changes says, "Former kings established myriad states and kept feudal lords close," and the Book of Documents says, "They harmonized the myriad states"—this is what is meant.

units.zh: 堯遭洪水，褱山襄陵，天下分絕，為十二州，使禹治之。
units.en: In Yao's time, the great flood surrounded the mountains and rose over the hills, cutting the realm into separate parts. Yao established twelve provinces and ordered Yu to bring the waters under control.
units.literal: When Yao faced the great flood, waters embraced mountains and overtopped hills, splitting the realm apart. He made twelve provinces and had Yu regulate them.

units.zh: 水土既平，更制九州，列五服，任土作貢。
units.en: Once waters and lands were leveled, he recast them as nine provinces, set out five service zones, and assigned tribute according to local produce.
units.literal: Once waters and lands were leveled, he recast them as nine provinces, set out five service zones, and assigned tribute according to local produce.

units.zh: 曰：禹敷土，隨山刊木，奠高山大川。
units.en: It says: Yu spread out the land, followed mountains and cut paths through woods, and fixed the high mountains and great rivers.
units.literal: It says: Yu spread out the land, followed mountains and cut paths through woods, and fixed the high mountains and great rivers.

units.zh: 冀州既載，壺口治梁及岐。
units.en: When Jizhou was set in order, Hukou was regulated, and work on Liang and Qi was completed.
units.literal: When Jizhou was surveyed, Hukou was regulated, and Liang and Qi were brought to completion.

units.zh: 既脩太原，至于嶽陽。
units.en: Taiyuan was repaired, reaching to the south of Mount Yue.
units.literal: Taiyuan was repaired, reaching to the south of Mount Yue.

units.zh: 覃懷底績，至于衡章。
units.en: Tanhuai was brought to completion, reaching Hengzhang.
units.literal: Tanhuai was brought to completion, reaching Hengzhang.

units.zh: 厥土惟白壤。
units.en: Its soil was white loam.
units.literal: Its soil was white loam.

units.zh: 厥賦上上錯，厥田中中。
units.en: Its levy was highest-high mixed rate; its fields were middle-middle.
units.literal: Its levy was highest-high mixed rate; its fields were middle-middle.

units.zh: 恆、衛既從，大陸既作。
units.en: The Heng and Wei rivers followed their courses; the Great Plain was restored.
units.literal: The Heng and Wei rivers followed their courses; the Great Plain was restored.

units.zh: 鳥夷皮服。
units.en: The Bird Yi wore skins as clothing.
units.literal: The Bird Yi wore skins as clothing.

units.zh: 夾右碣石，入于河。
units.en: Passing right of Jieshi cliffs, one entered the Yellow River.
units.literal: Passing right of Jieshi cliffs, one entered the Yellow River.

units.zh: 泲、河惟兗州。
units.en: Ji and Yellow formed Yanzhou.
units.literal: Ji and Yellow formed Yanzhou.

units.zh: 九河既道，雷夏既澤，雍、沮會同，桑土既蠶，是降丘宅土。
units.en: The Nine Rivers had been opened into channels, Leixia had become a marsh, and the Yong and Ju waters joined together. Mulberry lands were set to silkworm raising, and the people came down from the hills to settle the plains.
units.literal: The Nine Rivers were channeled, Leixia became marsh, Yong and Ju met and joined; mulberry lands raised silkworms, and people descended from hills to settle plains.

units.zh: 厥土黑墳，屮繇木條。
units.en: Its soil was dark, rich, and mounded; grasses and trees were lush and straight.
units.literal: Its soil was dark, rich, and mounded; grasses and trees were lush and straight.

units.zh: 厥田中下，賦貞，作十有三年乃同。
units.en: Its fields were middle-lower, levy fixed; after thirteen years they matched the standard.
units.literal: Its fields were middle-lower, levy fixed; after thirteen years they matched the standard.

units.zh: 厥貢漆絲，厥棐織文。
units.en: Its tribute was lacquer and silk, with patterned woven goods.
units.literal: Its tribute was lacquer and silk, with patterned woven goods.

units.zh: 浮于泲、漯，通于河。
units.en: They floated down Ji and Tuo to reach the Yellow River.
units.literal: They floated down Ji and Tuo to reach the Yellow River.

units.zh: 海、岱惟青州。
units.en: Sea and Tai formed Qingzhou.
units.literal: Sea and Tai formed Qingzhou.

units.zh: 嵎夷既略，惟、甾其道。
units.en: Yuyi was surveyed; the Wei and Zai rivers found their channels.
units.literal: Yuyi was surveyed; the Wei and Zai rivers found their channels.

units.zh: 厥土白墳，海瀕廣潟。
units.en: Its soil was white and rich, with broad saline flats by the sea.
units.literal: Its soil was white and rich, with broad saline flats by the sea.

units.zh: 田上下，賦中上。
units.en: Fields ranked upper-lower; levy middle-upper.
units.literal: Fields ranked upper-lower; levy middle-upper.

units.zh: 貢鹽、絺，海物惟錯，岱畎絲、枲、鈆、松、怪石，萊夷作牧，厥棐览絲。
units.en: Its tribute consisted of salt, fine cloth, and assorted products of the sea, together with silk, hemp, lead, pine, and unusual stones from the valleys of Tai. The Lai Yi tended livestock, and their tribute included dark silk floss.
units.literal: Tribute included salt and fine cloth, various sea products, silk, hemp, lead, pine, and rare stones from Tai valleys; Lai Yi herded stock, and their tribute included dark silk floss.

units.zh: 浮于汶，達于泲。
units.en: They floated down Wen and reached Ji.
units.literal: They floated down Wen and reached Ji.

units.zh: 海、岱及淮惟徐州。
units.en: Sea, Tai, and Huai formed Xuzhou.
units.literal: Sea, Tai, and Huai formed Xuzhou.

units.zh: 淮、沂其乂，蒙、羽其藝。
units.en: Huai and Yi were brought to order; Meng and Yu were cultivated.
units.literal: Huai and Yi were brought to order; Meng and Yu were cultivated.

units.zh: 大野既豬，東原厎平。
units.en: The Great Marsh was impounded and the eastern plain leveled.
units.literal: The Great Marsh was impounded and the eastern plain leveled.

units.zh: 厥土赤埴墳，草木漸包。
units.en: Its soil was red clay-rich loam, with grasses and trees increasingly dense.
units.literal: Its soil was red clay-rich loam, with grasses and trees increasingly dense.

units.zh: 田上中，賦中中。
units.en: Fields were upper-middle; levy middle-middle.
units.literal: Fields were upper-middle; levy middle-middle.

units.zh: 貢土五色，羽畎夏狄，嶧陽孤桐，泗瀕浮磬，淮夷蠙珠臮魚，厥棐玄纖縞。
units.en: The tribute was five-colored earth, bird plumes and summer pelts from the valleys, solitary paulownia from Yiyang, floating stone chimes from the banks of the Si, pearls and fish from the Huai Yi, and dark, fine silk gauze.
units.literal: Tribute was five-colored earth, bird plumes and summer pelts from valleys, lone paulownia from Yiyang, floating chimes from Si shores, pearls and fish from Huai Yi, and dark fine silk-gauze goods.

units.zh: 浮于淮、泗，達于河。
units.en: They floated down Huai and Si and reached the River.
units.literal: They floated down Huai and Si and reached the River.

units.zh: 淮、海惟揚州。
units.en: Huai and sea formed Yangzhou.
units.literal: Huai and sea formed Yangzhou.

units.zh: 彭蠡既豬，陽鳥逌居。
units.en: When Poyang was impounded, migratory birds settled there.
units.literal: When Poyang was impounded, migratory birds settled there.

units.zh: 三江既入，震澤厎定。
units.en: The Three Rivers entered their courses and Zhen Marsh was stabilized.
units.literal: The Three Rivers entered their courses and Zhen Marsh was stabilized.

units.zh: 篠簜既敷，魇夭木喬。
units.en: Bamboo and reeds spread; grasses flourished and trees grew tall.
units.literal: Bamboo and reeds had spread; grasses flourished and trees were tall.

units.zh: 厥土塗泥。
units.en: Its soil was muddy silt.
units.literal: Its soil was muddy silt.

units.zh: 田下下，賦下上錯。
units.en: Fields were lower-lower; levy lower-upper mixed.
units.literal: Fields were lower-lower; levy lower-upper mixed.

units.zh: 貢金三品，瑤、鲥、篠簜，齒、革、羽毛，鳥夷卉服，厥棐織貝，厥包橘、柚，錫貢。
units.en: The tribute included the three grades of metal, jade and fish products, bamboo and reeds, tusks, hides, feathers, and hair. The Bird Yi wore clothing of plant fiber; their woven tribute included shell-patterned cloth, and bundled oranges and pomelos were presented by special command.
units.literal: Tribute included three grades of metal, jade and fish products, bamboo and reeds, teeth, hides, feathers, and hair; Bird Yi wore plant fiber clothing; their woven tribute included shell-cloth; bundled oranges and pomelos were given by special command.

units.zh: 均江海，通于淮、泗。
units.en: They equalized routes by river and sea, connecting to Huai and Si.
units.literal: They equalized routes by river and sea, connecting to Huai and Si.

units.zh: 荊及衡陽惟荊州。
units.en: Jing and south of Heng formed Jingzhou.
units.literal: Jing and south of Heng formed Jingzhou.

units.zh: 江、漢朝宗于海。
units.en: The Yangtze and Han paid court to the sea.
units.literal: The Yangtze and Han paid court to the sea.

units.zh: 九江孔殷，沱、灊既道，雲夢，土作乂。
units.en: The Nine Rivers were abundant; Tuo and Qian were channeled; Yunmeng lands were brought into order.
units.literal: The Nine Rivers were abundant; Tuo and Qian were channeled; Yunmeng lands were brought into order.

units.zh: 厥土塗泥。
units.en: Its soil was muddy silt.
units.literal: Its soil was muddy silt.

units.zh: 田下中，賦上下。
units.en: Fields were lower-middle; levy upper-lower.
units.literal: Fields were lower-middle; levy upper-lower.

units.zh: 貢羽旄、齒、革，金三品，杶、幹、栝、柏，厲、砥、砮、丹，惟箘廐、楛，三國厎貢厥名，包匭菁茅，厥棐玄纁璣組，九江納錫大龜。
units.en: The tribute included feathers, yak tails, tusks, hides, the three grades of metal, various timbers, whetstones, arrow-stone, cinnabar, special bamboo and thorn woods, and named products from the three states. It also included bundled green thatch, dark-red woven strings with beads, and, from the Nine Rivers, a specially presented great turtle.
units.literal: Tribute included feathers, yak tails, teeth, hides, three grades of metal, various timbers, whetstones, arrow stones, cinnabar, special bamboo and thorn woods, and produce from three states; bundled green thatch, dark-red woven jewels and cords, and from Nine Rivers a specially offered great turtle.

units.zh: 浮于江、沱、灊、漢，逾于洛，至于南河。
units.en: They floated by Yangtze, Tuo, Qian, and Han, crossed to Luo, and reached the southern Yellow River.
units.literal: They floated by Yangtze, Tuo, Qian, and Han, crossed to Luo, and reached the southern Yellow River.

units.zh: 荊、河惟豫州。
units.en: Jing and River formed Yuzhou.
units.literal: Jing and River formed Yuzhou.

units.zh: 伊、雒、瀍、澗既入于河，滎、波既豬，道荷澤，被盟豬。
units.en: Yi, Luo, Chan, and Jian entered the River; Ying and Bo were impounded; waters reached He marsh and spread to Meng marsh.
units.literal: Yi, Luo, Chan, and Jian entered the River; Ying and Bo were impounded; waters reached He marsh and spread to Meng marsh.

units.zh: 厥土惟壤，下土墳壚。
units.en: Its soil was good loam, with lower lands of mounded black earth.
units.literal: Its soil was good loam, with lower lands of mounded black earth.

units.zh: 田中上，賦錯上中。
units.en: Fields were middle-upper; levy mixed upper-middle.
units.literal: Fields were middle-upper; levy mixed upper-middle.

units.zh: 貢漆、枲、絺、紵、棐纖纊，錫貢磬錯。
units.en: Tribute included lacquer, hemp, fine cloth, ramie, fine floss goods, and specially offered chime-stones of mixed type.
units.literal: Tribute included lacquer, hemp, fine cloth, ramie, fine floss goods, and specially offered chime-stones of mixed type.

units.zh: 浮于洛，入于河。
units.en: They floated down Luo and entered the River.
units.literal: They floated down Luo and entered the River.

units.zh: 華陽、黑水惟梁州。
units.en: South of Hua and Blackwater formed Liangzhou.
units.literal: South of Hua and Blackwater formed Liangzhou.

units.zh: 岷、嶓既藝，沱、灊既道，蔡、蒙旅平，和夷厎績。
units.en: Min and Bo were cultivated; Tuo and Qian were channeled; Cai and Meng districts leveled and Yi peoples made productive.
units.literal: Min and Bo were cultivated; Tuo and Qian were channeled; Cai and Meng districts leveled and Yi peoples made productive.

units.zh: 厥土青黎。
units.en: Its soil was blue-black.
units.literal: Its soil was blue-black.

units.zh: 田下上，賦下中三錯。
units.en: Fields were lower-upper; levy lower-middle with three mixed rates.
units.literal: Fields were lower-upper; levy lower-middle with three mixed rates.

units.zh: 貢璆、鐵、銀、鏤、砮、磬，熊、羆、狐、貍、織皮。
units.en: Its tribute comprised jade, iron, silver, inlaid work, arrow stones, and chime-stones, along with the hides of bears, brown bears, foxes, and civets.
units.literal: Tribute included jade, iron, silver, inlaid metalwork, arrow stones, and chime-stones, with hides of bears, brown bears, foxes, and civets.

units.zh: 西頃因桓是來，浮于灊，逾于沔，入于渭，亂于河。
units.en: From the western heights along the Huan route, tribute was floated on the Qian, carried across the Han, sent into the Wei, and conveyed to the Yellow River.
units.literal: From the western ranges they came by the Huan route; tribute floated on the Qian, crossed the Han, entered the Wei, and joined the Yellow River.

units.zh: 黑水、西河惟雍州。
units.en: Blackwater and west of the River formed Yongzhou.
units.literal: Blackwater and west of the River formed Yongzhou.

units.zh: 弱水既西，涇屬渭汭。
units.en: Weakwater turned west; Jing joined the Wei confluence.
units.literal: Weakwater turned west; Jing joined the Wei confluence.

units.zh: 漆、沮既從，酆水逌同。
units.en: Qi and Ju followed course; Feng waters joined together.
units.literal: Qi and Ju followed course; Feng waters joined together.

units.zh: 荊、岐既旅，終南、惇物，至于鳥鼠。
units.en: Jing and Qi mountains were traversed, from Zhongnan and Dunwu to Bird-Mouse mountain.
units.literal: Jing and Qi mountains were traversed, from Zhongnan and Dunwu to Bird-Mouse mountain.

units.zh: 原隰厎績，至于豬野。
units.en: Plains and wetlands were brought to completion, reaching Zhuye.
units.literal: Plains and wetlands were brought to completion, reaching Zhuye.

units.zh: 三危既宅，三苗丕敘。
units.en: Three-Wei were settled and the Three Miao greatly ordered.
units.literal: Three-Wei were settled and the Three Miao greatly ordered.

units.zh: 厥土黃壤。
units.en: Its soil was yellow loam.
units.literal: Its soil was yellow loam.

units.zh: 田上上，賦中下。
units.en: Fields were upper-upper; levy middle-lower.
units.literal: Fields were upper-upper; levy middle-lower.

units.zh: 貢球、琳、琅玕。
units.en: Tribute included jade globes, fine jades, and langgan gems.
units.literal: Tribute included jade globes, fine jades, and langgan gems.

units.zh: 浮于積石，至于龍門西河，會于渭汭。
units.en: They floated from Jishi to Longmen and the western Yellow River, joining at the Wei confluence.
units.literal: They floated from Jishi to Longmen and the western Yellow River, joining at the Wei confluence.

units.zh: 織皮昆崙、析支、渠叟，西戎即敘。
units.en: From woven hides came products of Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou; western Rong came into orderly submission.
units.literal: From woven hides came products of Kunlun, Xizhi, and Qusou; western Rong came into orderly submission.

units.zh: 道钐及岐，至于荊山，逾于河；
units.en: From Qian and Qi they went on to Jing Mountain and crossed the Yellow River;
units.literal: Following Qian and Qi, they reached Jing Mountain and crossed the River;

units.zh: 壺口、雷首，至于大嶽；
units.en: from Hukou and Leishou they reached Great Yue;
units.literal: from Hukou and Leishou they reached Great Yue;

units.zh: 厎柱、析城，至于王屋；
units.en: from Dizhu and Xicheng they reached Wangwu;
units.literal: from Dizhu and Xicheng they reached Wangwu;

units.zh: 太行、恆山，至于碣石，入于海。
units.en: from Taihang and Heng they reached Jieshi and entered the sea.
units.literal: from Taihang and Heng they reached Jieshi and entered the sea.

units.zh: 西傾、朱圉、鳥鼠，至于太華；
units.en: From Xiqing, Zhuyu, and Bird-Mouse they reached Great Hua;
units.literal: From Xiqing, Zhuyu, and Bird-Mouse they reached Great Hua;

units.zh: 熊耳、外方、桐柏，至于倍尾。
units.en: from Xionger, Waifang, and Tongbai they reached Beiwei.
units.literal: from Xionger, Waifang, and Tongbai they reached Beiwei.

units.zh: 道嶓冢，至于荊山；
units.en: Following Bo mound they reached Jing mountain;
units.literal: Following Bo mound they reached Jing mountain;

units.zh: 內方，至于大別；
units.en: from Neifang they reached Great Bie;
units.literal: from Neifang they reached Great Bie;

units.zh: 崏山之陽，至于衡山，過九江，至于敷淺原。
units.en: from south of Min mountain they reached Heng mountain, crossed Nine Rivers, and reached Fuzhanyuan.
units.literal: from south of Min mountain they reached Heng mountain, crossed Nine Rivers, and reached Fuzhanyuan.

units.zh: 道弱水，至于合藜，餘波入于流沙。
units.en: They guided Weakwater to Heli; remaining flow entered the shifting sands.
units.literal: They guided Weakwater to Heli; remaining flow entered the shifting sands.

units.zh: 道黑水，至于三危，入于南海。
units.en: They guided Blackwater to Three-Wei and into the southern sea.
units.literal: They guided Blackwater to Three-Wei and into the southern sea.

units.zh: 道河積石，至于龍門，南至于華陰，東至于厎柱，又東至于盟津，東過洛汭，至于大伾，北過降水，至于大陸，又北播為九河，同為逆河，入于海。
units.en: They channeled the Yellow River from Jishi to Longmen, south to Huayin, east to Dizhu, and farther east to Mengjin. It then passed east beyond the Luo confluence to Dapi, north past the Jiang waters to the Great Plain, and farther north divided into the Nine Rivers, which joined as the Reversing River and entered the sea.
units.literal: They guided the River from Jishi to Longmen, south to Huayin, east to Dizhu, further east to Mengjin, east past Luo confluence to Dapi, north past Jiang waters to the Great Plain, then north split into Nine Rivers, together called Reverse River, entering the sea.

units.zh: 嶓冢道漾，東流為漢，又東為滄浪之水，過三澨，至于大別，南入于江，東匯澤為彭蠡，東為北江，入于海。
units.en: From Bozhong they channeled the Yang waters eastward to become the Han, then farther east as the Canglang waters. Passing the Three Rapids, it reached Dabie, flowed south into the Yangtze, gathered eastward as Pengli, and then, as the North River, entered the sea.
units.literal: From Bo mound they guided Yang waters east as Han, then east as Canglang waters, past the three shoals to Great Bie, south into Yangtze, east gathering as Poyang, east as North River into the sea.

units.zh: 崏山道江，東別為沱，又東至于醴，過九江，至于東陵，東迆北會于匯，東為中江，入于海。
units.en: From Mount Min they channeled the Yangtze, which branched eastward as the Tuo, then flowed east to Li, passed the Nine Rivers to Dongling, wound east and north to join at Hui, and finally, as the Middle River, entered the sea.
units.literal: From Min mountain they guided Yangtze, branching east as Tuo, then east to Li, past Nine Rivers to Dongling, winding east and north to join at Hui, then east as Middle River into the sea.

units.zh: 道沇水，東流為泲，入于河，軼為滎，東出于陶丘北，又東至于荷，又東北會於汶，又北東入于海。
units.en: They channeled the Yan waters eastward as the Ji into the Yellow River. It overflowed as the Ying, emerged east north of Taoqiu, continued east to He, turned northeast to meet the Wen, and then flowed northeast into the sea.
units.literal: They guided Yan waters east as Ji into the River, overflowed as Ying, then east out north of Taoqiu, east to He, northeast to meet Wen, then north-east into the sea.

units.zh: 道淮自桐柏，東會于泗、沂，東入于海。
units.en: They guided Huai from Tongbai, east to meet Si and Yi, then east into the sea.
units.literal: They guided Huai from Tongbai, east to meet Si and Yi, then east into the sea.

units.zh: 道渭自鳥鼠同穴，東會于酆，又東至于涇，又東過漆、沮，入于河。
units.en: They guided Wei from Bird-Mouse common cave, east to meet Feng, then east to Jing, then east past Qi and Ju into the River.
units.literal: They guided Wei from Bird-Mouse common cave, east to meet Feng, then east to Jing, then east past Qi and Ju into the River.

units.zh: 道洛自熊耳，東北會于澗、瀍，又東會于伊，又東北入于河。
units.en: They guided Luo from Xionger, northeast to meet Jian and Chan, then east to meet Yi, then northeast into the River.
units.literal: They guided Luo from Xionger, northeast to meet Jian and Chan, then east to meet Yi, then northeast into the River.

units.zh: 九州逌同，四奧既宅，九山刊旅，九川滌原，九澤既陂，四海會同。
units.en: Thus the nine provinces were brought into accord, the four remote quarters were settled, the nine mountains were opened and traversed, the nine rivers were cleared to their sources, the nine marshes were embanked, and the four seas came together in common order.
units.literal: The nine provinces were thus harmonized; the four remote regions settled; the nine mountains traversed; the nine rivers dredged to source; the nine marshes embanked; and the four seas brought to common order.

units.zh: 六府孔修，庶土交正，厎慎財賦，咸則三壤，成賦中國。
units.en: The six resources were thoroughly ordered, the various soils were properly classified, and taxes and tribute were carefully set. All were measured according to the three grades of soil, completing the assessments for the central realm.
units.literal: The six treasuries were fully regulated, all soils correctly arranged, levies carefully managed, all by three soil grades, thereby completing tribute assessments of the central realm.

units.zh: 錫土姓：「祗台德先，不距朕行。」
units.en: He granted lands and surnames, declaring, "Reverently put virtue first; do not oppose what I intend to do."
units.literal: He granted lands and surnames, saying, "Reverently stand in virtue first; do not resist my undertakings."

units.zh: 五百里甸服：百里賦內總，二百里納銍，三百里內戛服，四百里粟，五百里米。
units.en: Within the five-hundred-li royal domain, the first hundred li paid bundled stalks, the second hundred li paid trimmed grain, the third hundred li paid husked grain, the fourth hundred li paid grain, and the fifth hundred li paid rice.
units.literal: Five hundred li of royal-domain service: at one hundred li, tribute of bundled grain stalks; at two hundred li, delivery of trimmed grain; at three hundred li, delivery of husked grain; at four hundred li, grain; at five hundred li, rice.

units.zh: 五百里侯服：百里采，二百里男國，三百里諸侯。
units.en: Five hundred li of Hou service: first hundred li were cai-fiefs, second hundred li were male states, third hundred li were feudal states.
units.literal: Five hundred li of Hou service: first hundred li were cai-fiefs, second hundred li were male states, third hundred li were feudal states.

units.zh: 五百里綏服：三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。
units.en: Five hundred li of Sui service: three hundred li measured by civil instruction, two hundred li by martial defense.
units.literal: Five hundred li of Sui service: three hundred li measured by civil instruction, two hundred li by martial defense.

units.zh: 五百里要服：三百里夷，二百里蔡。
units.en: Five hundred li of the constrained service zone: three hundred li of the Yi zone, two hundred li of the Cai zone.
units.literal: Five hundred li of constrained service: three hundred li of Yi, two hundred li of Cai.

units.zh: 五百里荒服：三百里蠻，二百里流。
units.en: Five hundred li of Huang service: three hundred li Man, two hundred li exile zones.
units.literal: Five hundred li of Huang service: three hundred li Man, two hundred li exile zones.

units.zh: 東漸于海，西被于流沙，朔、南臮，聲教訖于四海。
units.en: It reached the sea in the east, the shifting sands in the west, and the northern and southern extremities alike, until the civilizing influence had spread to the four seas.
units.literal: To the east it reached the sea; to the west it extended to the shifting sands; to north and south alike; and the transforming influence extended to the four seas.

units.zh: 禹錫玄圭，告厥成功。
units.en: Yu received the dark jade tablet and announced his success.
units.literal: Yu received the dark jade tablet and announced his success.

units.zh: 後受禪於虞，為夏后氏。
units.en: He then received the abdication from Shun and founded the house of Xia.
units.literal: Later he received the abdication from Shun and became the Xia sovereign.

units.zh: 殷因於夏，亡所變改。
units.en: Shang inherited from Xia and changed nothing substantial.
units.literal: Shang inherited from Xia and changed nothing substantial.

units.zh: 周既克殷，監於二代而損益之，定官分職，改禹徐、梁二州合之於雍、青，分冀州之地以為幽、并。
units.en: After overthrowing the Shang, the Zhou court adapted earlier institutions, reorganized offices and responsibilities, folded Xu and Liang into Yong and Qing, and carved You and Bing out of Ji Province.
units.literal: After Zhou had conquered Yin, it took lessons from the previous two dynasties, reducing and augmenting their institutions, fixed offices and divided duties, merged Yu's Xu and Liang Provinces into Yong and Qing, and split Ji Province to create You and Bing.

units.zh: 故周官有職方氏，掌天下之地，辯九州之國。
units.en: So the Zhou established an office in charge of territorial administration, tasked with classifying the states of the nine provinces.
units.literal: Therefore in Zhou administration there was the Director of Regions, who managed the lands under Heaven and distinguished the states of the nine provinces.

units.zh: 東南曰揚州：其山曰會稽，藪曰具區，川曰三江，寖曰五湖；
units.en: The southeastern region was Yang Province, marked by Mount Kuaiji, the Juqu marsh, the Three Rivers, and the Five Lakes.
units.literal: The southeast is called Yang Province: its mountain is Kuaiji, its marsh is Juqu, its rivers are the Three Rivers, its inundations are the Five Lakes.

units.zh: 其利金、錫、竹箭；
units.en: Its chief products were gold, tin, and bamboo for arrows.
units.literal: Its resources are gold, tin, and bamboo arrows.

units.zh: 民二男五女；
units.en: Its population ratio was recorded as two men for every five women.
units.literal: Its people are two men to five women.

units.zh: 畜宜鳥獸，穀宜稻。
units.en: The area favored fowl and game, and its staple grain was rice.
units.literal: Its livestock are suited to birds and beasts, and its grain is suited to rice.

units.zh: 正南曰荊州：其山曰衡，藪曰雲夢，川曰江、漢，寖曰潁、湛；
units.en: Directly south lay Jing Province, defined by Mount Heng, the Yunmeng marshes, the Yangtze and Han rivers, and the Ying and Zhan waters.
units.literal: Due south is called Jing Province: its mountain is Heng, its marsh is Yunmeng, its rivers are the Yangtze and Han, its inundations are the Ying and Zhan.

units.zh: 其利丹、銀、齒、革；
units.en: Its noted products were cinnabar, silver, ivory, and leather.
units.literal: Its resources are cinnabar, silver, ivory, and hides.

units.zh: 民一男二女；
units.en: Its recorded sex ratio was one man to two women.
units.literal: Its people are one man to two women.

units.zh: 畜及穀宜，與揚州同。
units.en: Its livestock and crops matched those of Yang Province.
units.literal: Its livestock and grains are suitable, the same as Yang Province.

units.zh: 河南曰豫州：其山曰華，藪曰圃田，川曰滎、雒，簧曰波、溠；
units.en: The region south of the Yellow River was Yu Province, with Mount Hua, the Putian marsh, the Ying and Luo rivers, and the Bo and Cha waterways.
units.literal: South of the Yellow River is called Yu Province: its mountain is Hua, its marsh is Putian, its rivers are Ying and Luo, its watercourses are Bo and Cha.

units.zh: 其利林、漆、絲枲；
units.en: Its valuable products included timber, lacquer, silk, and hemp.
units.literal: Its resources are timber, lacquer, silk, and hemp.

units.zh: 民二男三女；
units.en: Its ratio was listed as two men for every three women.
units.literal: Its people are two men to three women.

units.zh: 畜宜六擾，其穀宜五種。
units.en: It supported all six domestic animals and all five principal grains.
units.literal: Its livestock suit the six domestic animals; its grains suit the five kinds.

units.zh: 正東曰青州：其山曰沂，藪曰孟諸，川曰淮、泗，寖曰沂、沭；
units.en: To the east was Qing Province, identified with Mount Yi, the Mengzhu marsh, the Huai and Si rivers, and the Yi and Shu waters.
units.literal: Due east is called Qing Province: its mountain is Yi, its marsh is Mengzhu, its rivers are Huai and Si, its inundations are Yi and Shu.

units.zh: 其利蒲、魚；
units.en: Its chief products were reeds and fish.
units.literal: Its resources are reeds and fish.

units.zh: 民二男三女；
units.en: Its recorded ratio was two men to three women.
units.literal: Its people are two men to three women.

units.zh: 其畜宜雞、狗，穀宜稻、麥。
units.en: It was suited to raising chickens and dogs, and to growing rice and wheat.
units.literal: Its livestock suit chickens and dogs; its grains suit rice and wheat.

units.zh: 河東曰兗州：其山曰岱，藪曰泰野，其川曰河、泲，浸曰盧、濰；
units.en: East of the Yellow River lay Yan Province, with Mount Tai, the Taiye marsh, the Yellow and Ji rivers, and the Lu and Wei waters.
units.literal: East of the Yellow River is called Yan Province: its mountain is Tai, its marsh is Taiye, its rivers are the Yellow River and Ji, its inundations are Lu and Wei.

units.zh: 其利蒲、魚；
units.en: Its key products were reeds and fish.
units.literal: Its resources are reeds and fish.

units.zh: 民二男三女；
units.en: Its ratio was two men for every three women.
units.literal: Its people are two men to three women.

units.zh: 其畜宜六擾，穀宜四種。
units.en: It supported all six domestic animals and four major grains.
units.literal: Its livestock suit the six domestic animals; its grains suit four kinds.

units.zh: 正西曰雍州：其山曰嶽，藪曰弦蒲，川曰涇、汭，其浸曰渭、洛；
units.en: To the west was Yong Province, marked by Mount Yue, the Xianpu marsh, the Jing and Rui rivers, and the Wei and Luo waters.
units.literal: Due west is called Yong Province: its mountain is Yue, its marsh is Xianpu, its rivers are Jing and Rui, its inundations are Wei and Luo.

units.zh: 其利玉、石；
units.en: Its valued materials were jade and stone.
units.literal: Its resources are jade and stone.

units.zh: 其民三男二女；
units.en: Its ratio was recorded as three men to two women.
units.literal: Its people are three men to two women.

units.zh: 畜宜牛、馬，穀宜黍、稷。
units.en: It favored cattle and horses, and grew millet and broomcorn millet.
units.literal: Its livestock suit oxen and horses; its grains suit millet and broomcorn millet.

units.zh: 東北曰幽州：其山曰醫無閭，藪曰豯養，川曰河、泲，浸曰菑、時；
units.en: In the northeast was You Province, with Mount Yiwulu, the Xiyang marsh, the Yellow and Ji rivers, and the Zi and Shi waters.
units.literal: Northeast is called You Province: its mountain is Yiwulu, its marsh is Xiyang, its rivers are the Yellow River and Ji, its inundations are Zi and Shi.

units.zh: 其利魚、鹽；
units.en: Its chief products were fish and salt.
units.literal: Its resources are fish and salt.

units.zh: 民一男三女；
units.en: Its recorded ratio was one man to three women.
units.literal: Its people are one man to three women.

units.zh: 畜宜四擾，穀宜三種。
units.en: It was suitable for four types of domestic animals and three principal grains.
units.literal: Its livestock suit four domestic animals; its grains suit three kinds.

units.zh: 河內曰冀州：其山曰霍，藪曰揚紆，川曰漳，浸曰汾、潞；
units.en: The inner Yellow River region was Ji Province, marked by Mount Huo, the Yangyu marsh, the Zhang River, and the Fen and Lu waters.
units.literal: Within the Yellow River is called Ji Province: its mountain is Huo, its marsh is Yangyu, its river is Zhang, its inundations are Fen and Lu.

units.zh: 其利松、柏；
units.en: Its valued timber was pine and cypress.
units.literal: Its resources are pine and cypress.

units.zh: 民五男三女；
units.en: Its ratio was listed as five men to three women.
units.literal: Its people are five men to three women.

units.zh: 畜宜牛、羊，穀宜黍、稷。
units.en: It favored cattle and sheep, with millet and broomcorn millet as staple crops.
units.literal: Its livestock suit oxen and sheep; its grains suit millet and broomcorn millet.

units.zh: 正北曰并州：其山曰恆山，藪曰昭餘祁，川曰虖池、嘔夷，浸曰淶、易；
units.en: To the north was Bing Province, with Mount Heng, the Zhaoyuqi marsh, the Huchi and Ouyi rivers, and the Lai and Yi waters.
units.literal: Due north is called Bing Province: its mountain is Mount Heng, its marsh is Zhaoyuqi, its rivers are Huchi and Ouyi, its inundations are Lai and Yi.

units.zh: 其利布帛；
units.en: Its notable products were cloth and silk textiles.
units.literal: Its resources are cloth and silk fabrics.

units.zh: 民二男三女；
units.en: Its ratio was two men for every three women.
units.literal: Its people are two men to three women.

units.zh: 畜宜五擾，穀宜五種。
units.en: It supported five kinds of livestock and all five major grains.
units.literal: Its livestock suit five domestic animals; its grains suit five kinds.

units.zh: 而保章氏掌天文，以星土辯九州之地，所封封域皆有分星，以視吉凶。
units.en: The court officer of Bao Zhang oversaw astronomy, mapping the nine provinces to their corresponding stars so that each fief's allotted constellation could be used to read good and ill fortune.
units.literal: The Bao Zhang officer administered astronomy, using the stars of each territory to distinguish the lands of the nine provinces; every enfeoffed domain had its allotting star, by which fortune and misfortune were observed.

units.zh: 周爵五等，而土三等：公、侯百里，伯七十里，子、男五十里。
units.en: The Zhou nobility had five ranks, but fiefs came in three standard sizes: 100 li for dukes and marquises, 70 for earls, and 50 for viscounts and barons.
units.literal: Zhou had five ranks of nobility, while lands had three grades: dukes and marquises had one hundred li, earls had seventy li, viscounts and barons had fifty li.

units.zh: 不滿為附庸，蓋千八百國。
units.en: Smaller polities were treated as dependencies, bringing the total to roughly 1,800 states.
units.literal: Those below that were dependent states; in all there were about 1,800 states.

units.zh: 而太昊、黃帝之後，唐、虞侯伯猶存，帝王圖籍相踵而可知。
units.en: Descendant lines from legendary rulers and from Tang and Yu still survived, and the successive records of emperors and kings make this traceable.
units.literal: And the descendants of Taihao and Yellow Emperor, and the lords and earls of Tang and Yu, still existed; imperial and royal records followed one after another and can be known.

units.zh: 周室既衰，禮樂征伐自諸侯出，轉相吞滅，數百年間，列國秏盡。
units.en: Once Zhou authority weakened, power shifted to the feudal lords, who conquered one another until the old roster of states was nearly wiped out over a few centuries.
units.literal: After the Zhou house declined, rites, music, campaigns, and punishments issued from the feudal lords; they swallowed one another, and over several hundred years the listed states were exhausted.

units.zh: 至春秋時，尚有數十國，五伯迭興，總其盟會。
units.en: In Spring and Autumn times, dozens of states remained, and the Five Hegemons took turns dominating interstate alliances.
units.literal: By the Spring and Autumn period there were still several dozen states; the Five Hegemons rose in turn and led their alliances.

units.zh: 陵夷至於戰國，天下分而為七，合從連衡，經數十年。
units.en: By the Warring States era, the world had fractured into seven powers that maneuvered through shifting alliance blocs for decades.
units.literal: Declining further into the Warring States, the realm split into seven; vertical and horizontal alliances lasted for decades.

units.zh: 秦遂并兼四海。
units.en: Qin eventually conquered and unified the empire.
units.literal: Qin then annexed and united all under Heaven.

units.zh: 以為周制微弱，終為諸侯所喪，故不立尺土之封，分天下為郡縣，盪滅前聖之苗裔，靡有孑遺者矣。
units.en: Judging Zhou-style enfeoffment too weak, Qin refused to grant hereditary fiefs, reorganized the realm into commanderies and counties, and all but eradicated the old noble lineages.
units.literal: It considered Zhou institutions weak and ultimately lost to the feudal lords, so it established no enfeoffed lands even one chi wide, divided the realm into commanderies and counties, and swept away the descendants of former sages, leaving virtually none.

units.zh: 漢興，因秦制度，崇恩德，行簡易，以撫海內。
units.en: When the Han was founded, it largely inherited Qin institutions but governed with lighter, more humane policies to settle the realm.
units.literal: When Han arose, it followed Qin institutions, esteemed grace and virtue, and practiced simplicity and ease to pacify the empire.

units.zh: 至武帝攘卻胡、越，開地斥境，南置交阯，北置朔方之州，兼徐、梁、幽、并夏、周之制，改雍曰涼，改梁曰益，凡十三郡，置刺史。
units.en: Under Emperor Wu, campaigns against the Xiongnu and Yue expanded Han territory. Jiaozhi was established in the south and Shuofang in the north; provincial lines were adjusted, and thirteen inspection regions were ultimately set up under cishi inspectors.
units.literal: By Emperor Wu, he repelled Hu and Yue, opened lands and expanded frontiers, established Jiaozhi in the south and Shuofang province in the north, combined the Xia and Zhou arrangements of Xu, Liang, You, and Bing, changed Yong to Liang and Liang to Yi; in all thirteen provinces were set with regional inspectors.

units.zh: 先王之跡既遠，地名又數改易，是以采獲舊聞，考跡詩書，推表山川，以綴禹貢、周官、春秋，下及戰國、秦、漢焉。
units.en: Because ancient records were remote and place names had shifted repeatedly, this account gathers old traditions, checks them against the Classics, and maps mountains and rivers from the Yu Gong and Zhou institutions down through the Warring States, Qin, and Han.
units.literal: Since the traces of former kings are distant and place names have repeatedly changed, therefore old reports were collected, tracks in the Odes and Documents examined, mountains and rivers inferred and tabulated, to connect the Yu Tribute, Zhou Offices, and Spring and Autumn, down to Warring States, Qin, and Han.

units.literal: Counties (12): Chang'an, Xinfeng, Chuan Sikong, Lantian, Huayin, Zheng, Hu, Xiagui, Nanling, Fengming, Baling, Duling.

units.literal: Left Fengyi: households 235,101; population 917,822.

units.en: Hongnong Commandery counted 118,091 households and 475,954 people.

units.literal: Hedong Commandery: households 236,896; population 962,912.
